SYMPTOM: fullScreenCover opens and immediately dismisses on first launch. Works on subsequent attempts. Classic sign: `showExercise = true` fires before `exerciseViewModel` propagates, hits the nil branch which sets `showExercise = false`.

CAUSE: SwiftUI race condition when setting two @State vars in sequence:
```swift
// BROKEN - two-state race
exerciseViewModel = vm  // state 1
showExercise = true    // state 2 — closure evaluates before state 1 propagates
```
The `fullScreenCover(isPresented:)` closure can evaluate with `exerciseViewModel` still nil.

FIX: Use `fullScreenCover(item:)` with a single Identifiable source of truth:
```swift
// Make VM Identifiable
class ExerciseSessionViewModel: Identifiable { ... }

// One-state binding — no race possible
.fullScreenCover(item: $exerciseViewModel) { vm in
    ExerciseSessionView(viewModel: vm)
}
// To open: just set exerciseViewModel = vm
```

PREVENT: Whenever a fullScreenCover depends on a companion @State object (isPresented + content), use fullScreenCover(item:) instead.
